Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193B (Permit # 021-20850), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. • The well appears to be not in use. • The well valves are open and the surface is rusted entirely. • The well head appears intact with no signs of leaking. • OGI used an RKI GX-3R Pro to detect for the presence of gas and no gas was detected. • The 2023 annual production and mechanical assessment reports have not been submitted. • The most recent production report of 2019 indicated the well "Active" - Well Temporarily not producing. • The department requests the operator provide proof of production of the well or when it was last in use. Based on today’s inspections the following violations will be issued: Posting OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install permit number on well. MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. APR 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department.

properties.content:

Violation Code: 78A55(I)5I_ - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning – Operator’s emergency response plan failed to incorporate National Incident Management System planning standards, including the use of the Incident Command System, Incident Action Planning and Common Communications Plans.
Violation ID: 8267870
Permit API: 059-25724
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/18/2026
Comments: On 03/18/2026, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Mohr B Well Pad in Cumberland Township, Greene County. I was acompanied by Sara Trio (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist). Previously the Department issued violations for a spill reported to the Department (SAIR 4139769 Enf 452846).Violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2 were issued on 2/10/2026 for the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan onsite. The quantity was approximately 1-3 barrels.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 1).The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).A violation of 78A55(I)5I was issued on 02/10/2026 (SAIR 4139769 Enf 452846). In the operator's response, they stated the PPC and Emergency Response Plan are in a mailbox by cattle gates closer to Mohr A and Mohr B well pad. A mailbox with documents was at the gate along the access road. However, the mailbox and some of the binders were on the ground. The binders on the ground were not legible and damaged due to exposure to weather. In certain weather conditions, the mailbox and documents may be obstructed from view (Photos 3-5). I recommend the documents be reprinted and placed in a visible area off of the ground. A small amount of liquid was observed in the containment. The secondary containment for the tanks appeared to be emptied since my last inspection. (Photo 6). A conductivity reading taken in the gravel near the separator was 80.1 S/cm (Photo 7). I did not observe any couductivity readings in mS/cm.The production equipment appeared to be back in original position and the gravel pit has been filled (Photos 8-9). It appears the remediation process is complete. The operator is in compliance with schedule regarding the violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a66(b)2. The violation of 78A55(I)5I, issued on 02/10/2026 (SAIR 4139769 Enf 452846), remains outstanding.

Report Details

Violation ID: 973222
Permit API: 035-21329
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/24/2022
Comments: On October 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. DEP spoke with Profrac Company Man Mike Reel and he said they were fracking the 1005H well at the time of inspection. The DEP observed multiple areas of staining adjacent to the containment for the fracking rig. The areas were screened for conductivity with a soil conductivity meter and two areas resulted in over range conductivity readings. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4.0 mS/cm. The first area is adjacent to the frack pumps off the east side of containment. This area of high conductivity is about 12' x 20'. The second area is adjacent to 1 frac tank and 2 gas buster tanks. This area of high conductivity is about 10'x10'. Soil sample 0651-139 was collected from the 10'x10' area. The volume of this spill is unknown because it is uncertain how much was spilled under the frack rig containment. The DEP pointed out the previously mentioned areas to Mr. Reel and he said he would have someone begin scraping up the areas immediately. DEP then placed a phone call to STL Resources Seth Rodriguez to inform him of the findings from the inspection. The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductivity and updating DEP of the findings. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, the DEP recommends pursuing an Act 2 remediation. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in either of the stormwater vaults. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.2 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 3 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 31.7 uS/cm. Seep 4 was not screened due to the current condition of the seep screening area. This area is being driven through by ATVs checking on the freshwater waterline for the Sturgis South stimulation. The area is constantly being driven through to refuel the pumps on the waterline. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 24.7 uS/cm. The infiltration berms 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 11 along the access road are well vegetated and appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berms 1, 4, 6, 7, and 9 along the access road are vegetated but, the areas that are holding water have little vegetation and do not appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 1 off the northwest corner of the pad appears to be holding water and not functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 2 off the northwest corner of the pad and the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the pad are lacking vegetation in the infiltration area. The DEP recommends working on the infiltration berms that are not functioning correctly and reseeding the infiltration berms that are lacking vegetation to prevent an erosion event. The areas of staining along with the elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment on the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834

Inspection Date: 1/27/2026
Comments: On 1/27/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the JKLM Belz 2001 well pad located in Tioga Twp, Tioga Co. It was 10 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived at the location. Heavy snowfall has impacted the region within the last 48 hours. When I arrived on site, I started at JKLM's on-site office where the company man, Nick Peluso, explained current operations. A Highland rig has completed the surface sections to 800' and intermediate sections to 2700' on all six wells. The rig was currently drilling the kickoff for the tangent on the 12HM well and will drill the tangents on all six wells to between 4000' and 6000'. The rig will also drill a vertical pilot hole on the 6HM well, drilling to the Marcellus formation. After tests on the pilot well are conducted, the hole will be cemented back to the kickoff with the rig then drilling the tangent. After drilling all tangents, the Highland top-hole rig will be towered down and a bigger drilling rig will be mobilized to the site to finish drilling each well to total depth. The date for the big rig is yet to be determined. JKLM's Terra Tokarz accompanied me on the site inspection. Secondary containment had been installed around the well cellars with drilling operations being conducted within the secondary containment. Four half-round dumpsters had been installed in secondary containment to collect drill cuttings, another half-round dumpster was delivered during the inspection but had not been positioned prior to my departure. Drill cuttings were being solidified with wood chips. Two frac tanks and two 400-barrel tanks were installed on the north side of the pad, to be used for freshwater. Two 400-barrel tanks had been installed on the southeast side of the pad to be used for storing screened drilling water that had been used down hole. One 400-barrel brine tank has been installed on the southeast side. I observed the approximate area where a release was reported on 12/16/2025 in DEP inspection #4110167. Ice and snow was observed in this area and conductivity readings were not collected.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed around the pad. Two sediment basins have been installed on the west side of the pad. They appeared to be functioning as designed. Due to snow cover, site stabilization could not be assessed during this inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 4110167 for puddles of fluid with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface.The DEP recommends monitoring the site for released fluids and elevated conductance liquids and removing as discovered.I departed the site at 1400 hours.

Comments: The operator contacted the Department on Monday, September 16 to report a spill that was found at the Warrant 5573 W87 well site. This site was previously impacted by a 10+ barrel spill that occurred 8/4/16 (ID #2509096). The operator at the time, SWEPI LP, has since sold the well to Pennhills Resources, who is currently operating the well. SWEPI LP is remediating the site under the Department's Oil and Gas Spill Policy. Present on site for this inspection were DEP ECB representative Barry Stanton, Pennhills Resources' Stuart and Tom Morris, and SWEPI LP's Pat Bernethy, and myself. An unknown, but likely small, volume of oil leaked from a line at the site and leached down through rock and into a seep on the hillside below. A small amount of oil was visible in two siphon dams constructed as containment just below the site, as well as in a channel leading to a previously constructed siphon dam. A small amount of this oil was found leaking into an UNT of a Chappel Fork that was previously impacted. The total length of impact from the spill site is approximately 400 horizontal feet. The operator has dug up the line to determine where the leak occurred, and is collecting oil on absorbent pads. Discussion was made regarding the responsibility of each party regarding remediation and reporting. Further inspection will be done on this site as necessary.

Tighe Truman, a representative from Seneca Resources, was on site at the time of the inspection. He inferred the contaminated waste would be tested and taken to a local landfill to be properly disposed of. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of a possible spill/breached containment at the Beechwood Pad A site. (CTS #348135). The site was inspected for evidence of lack of secondary containment around equipment and/or spills. The production fluid tank site was inspected. This site contains three 400 barrel tanks. It appears from the staining on the tanks that they have overflowed at some point. The containment is filled with snow that has not fully melted. The area behind (on the north side) of the tank site was checked and there was some liquid beneath the ice in the ditch. This liquid measured between 2 mS/cm to over 6 mS/cm conductivity on the Spectrum Soil EC probe. It appears as though a leak occurred at this site at some point, which the operator allowed to escape containment through some means and enter the ditch line. The overflow detection system appears to have been turned off at this tank site. Also on site was a gas/liquid separator which was fed by several types of fluid. The fluids were contained in their separate containments. The separator was set in containment that had blocks set up for holding tanks that have been removed. The containment itself was dry and it was noted that there were several holes in the liner, which would allow any spilled fluid to leak out of containment. The area around the wellheads is clean and no evidence of spills was noted. The site ID sign is on site with well and pad information.

Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-25741 on January 28, 2025. The well site was snow covered. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, a small hole was observed on the back side of the brine tank (pictures 4 and 5). No visible fluids were observed trickling out of the hole, but the tank appears full up to that hole. No visible fluids were observed on the ground in the snow but there is evidence that the tank has been leaking. Orange staining was observed from the brine leak, there is an indentation in the ground directly below the leak, and a path of deer tracks lead up to the leaking brine tank. Please note, that I was unable to collect a soil sample due to frozen conditions. Violations have been cited.

An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/12/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/12/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 942385
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/12/2022
Comments: On January 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. At the time of inspection, contractors where excavating the area in front of the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the well pad. The depth of the excavation was about 4 to 5 ft. The area of the infiltration berm that had yet to be excavated had a conductivity greater than 4,000 uS/cm. The design of the trench along the west end of the pad caused production fluid to flow to the southwest corner also. The southwest area of the pad also has a drainage culvert with the outlet pipe draining to the infiltration berm. The pooled production fluid in the northwest infiltration berm has been vacuumed out. The conductivity of the soil in front of that infiltration berm was over 4,000 uS/cm. No excavation has been done to this area. The northwest plunge pool filled back with water. The conductivity of the water was over 4,000 uS/cm. A sample was collected from the plunge pool and will be analyzed for SAC code 942. Mr. Rodriguez thinks that the seal around the outlet pipe from the drainage culvert in that area is failing, resulting in water in the plunge pool. There were no new seeps or areas where the production fluid has appeared off the well pad edge. STL Resources plans to finish removing the impacted soil from the southwest infiltration berm and move to the northwest infiltration berm to begin removing impacted soil there. Mr. Rodriguez said that a vacuum truck was scheduled to vacuum out the water in the northwest plunge pool and the water that had drained into the culverts from the trench along the west end of the pad. The spill of production fluid off the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 401. Clean Streams Law 402(b) is being supplanted by Clean Streams Law 401. Violations from Inspection Report 3305227 remain outstanding.

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/07/2026
Comments: On April 7 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the H C McCullough 2 OG Well in regards to CTS 396257. Present during the inspection was Matt Woods (PADEP) and Darren Reilly (PADEP).The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the well appeared to be equipped for production. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it which contained the well name and API. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges from the wellhead were observed at the surface. A production tank was observed onsite. Affixed to the production tank was a well posting which appeared to contain all required information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H).Upon inspection of the production tank and associated piping, the Department observed what appeared to be a crack in the dump-line leading to the production tank. Under the apparent crack, the Department observed dark oil-like staining on the ground. The Department did not observe any fluid actively leaking from the cracked pipe at the time of the inspection. Conductivity readings of 0.07mS and 0.14mS were obtained in the area of dark staining. These readings appear comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.16mS. While the conductivity readings do not suggest a brine release has occurred, it still appears a release (most likely hydrocarbon/oil based) is occurring/has occurred onsite.Prior to leaving the site, the Department contacted operator representative Heather Empfield via phone call. The Department informed Ms. Empfield of the observed crack in the piping as well as the staining on the ground directly beneath. Ms. Emfield stated field crews would assess the site and remediate any release as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "DCNR 587 017" Marcellus well site.Megan DePue (Repsol, Remediation and Reclamation) called the DEP today to report that Pete Lorson (Repsol, Facilities) discovered an estimated 10 gallons of drilling mud leaked thru liner containment onto the gravel pad surface. Comments: On 08/25/2025, a complaint inspection was conducted at the plugged Blum 1 Well Site following receipt of a complaint (CTS 391464). The well was plugged on 12/12/2019. The permit number on the monument was incorrect and should read 37-125-22119-00. It appears that several pieces of casing remain at the plugging location (Photos 1-3).I observed several spots of oil/grease on the ground around the plugged well and what appears to be a demolished compressor station or dehydration system (Photos 4-9).The well site around the plugged well was not completely restored to original contour and vegetated. The adjacent compressor station was demolished, however equipment was present and piping remained. Pipes and electrical equipment were sticking out of the ground (Photos 2, 10-17).The access road was restored but appears to still be used (Photos 18, 19).The area where production tanks were previously, as seen on aerial imagery, displayed bare dirt (Photos 20-22). The tanks were not noted. Conductivity readings were obtained and no elevated readings were noted.The Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator following plugging. I recommend that the WSRR is submitted. Due to the operator failing to submit a WSRR within 60 days after restoration of the well site, failure to restore the site to original conditions, and failure to remove equipment/facilities, violations of 78.65(3), OGA3216(A), and OGA3216(D) are being issued.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/25/2023 at 0820 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted to summarize recent remedial activities since the last follow-up inspection on 4/10/2023 regarding a release from 4/6/2023. Blackhill has now had the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure removed from the impacted area. All material in this area that Blackhill discovered to have elevated electrical conductivity (EC) has been excavated (photos #1 and 2) and placed within lined waste containers or on secondary containment and covered (photo #3). I field measured water collected in the accessible portions of the excavated area shown in photos #1 and 2 and received readings of ~1.7mS/cm. Blackhill continues to have water that collects in these areas pumped out. The produced water tanks have been moved to a new location along the northern edge of the pad with a new secondary containment structure (photo #7). The yellow bin that holds the offload valve has now been placed further back so the entire bin is within secondary containment. Blackhill reported that elevated EC water was discovered along the buried produced water flowline. Portions of the pad material where the flowline was buried have now been excavated to a point where it can be done safely. The buried produced water flowline closest to the processing equipment has been "pot-holed" and elevated EC readings of ~2.7mS/cm were reported. Blackhill is in the process of devising a plan to continue excavation along the buried flowline safely.The entire southeastern stormwater basin (photo #4) has been excavated and Blackhill reported that field readings within the basin were now below 1.0mS/cm. A portion of the southern stormwater conveyance channel has been lined with plastic (photo #6) and a large sump was constructed just before the stormwater basin (photo #5). Blackhill reported that water collecting in the lined sump has been field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Blackhill is currently having stormwater collected from the excavated areas and secondary containments onsite following numerous rain events over the past few days.All violations associated with the release from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1000 hours.

Violation ID: 860402
Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-27
Comments: Follow-up inspection to assess overall conditions. Sean VanFleet, DEP, accompanied me on this inspection. I met with Rockdale company man Jim Tracey upon my arrival on location. Jim informed me that there would be a secondary containment contractor coming out later in the day to take up secondary containment in order to check for holes. The electrical conductivity (EC) in the sump rose slightly from the inspection the previous day. The EC is 9.14 mS/cm here. The EC in the sump in the NE basin remained steady at 900 mS/cm. The blue upright tank near the northeast corner of the pad remains in insufficient containment. The EC of the water on the pad surface continues to rise even when personnel on location say that no additives, like calcium chloride and lime, were being used. The Department recommends further investigation into the source of the increasing electrical conductivity. The Department recommends improving general housekeeping practices in order to prevent possible releases of regulated substances to the pad surface. The Department recommends considering alternative stormwater management practices that would prevent stormwater from getting to the northeast corner of the pad. Redirecting stormwater away from this corner could lead to a significant decrease in the amount of elevated conductivity fluid that has to be dealt with. The Department recommends vacuuming up elevated conductivity fluid on and off containment as frequently as is necessary. Outstanding violations. Violations pending sample results.

Comments: On March 27, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Shotski 7H well in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 3/25/2023. The report indicted that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released from a washed out pipe within GPU 7.The Act 9 site ID, PPC plan and ER plan were on site.At the time of inspection the Operator was decommissioning the GPUs. According to the on site representative the GPUs will be removed from the location and replaced.I observed staining and excavation around the 7H GPU. I utilized a conductivity probe to collect readings within the impacted area (photos 7,8 and 9).The impacted area appeared to be approximately 20' wide and 40' long and 2 to 12 inched in depth. I also collected a conductivity reading within the 7H self contained GPU (photo 13).The release appears to be contained to the well pad surface. Violation are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid and failure to design and construct the well site with secondary containment.

An Act 9 sign, site plans and inspection log remain in place at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted to evaluate an area of pooled fluids outside of secondary containment that returned elevated electrical conductivity readings during an inspection on 3/11/2025. During the inspection on 3/11/2025, the DEP collected a sample (#0983-469) and the analytical results determined that evidence of pollution was located outside of secondary containment. The results from sample #0983-469 are attached to this inspection as a file. Blackhill Energy reported that a total of ~14.6 gallons of fluids were recovered from the entire pad surface. During today's inspection, pooled fluids located in the area of concern were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 190 to 850us/cm. The area has been cleaned up to visible.Based on the findings of inspection record #3935064, the analytical sample results from DEP sample #0983-469 and the findings of this inspection, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23931 as immediately corrected:SWMA 301 and 25 Pa.
